title: Impact of SEC Investigation Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology using the market model to calculate abnormal returns and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR). The key assumption is that in the absence of the SEC investigation announcement, stock returns would follow the normal relationship with market returns as captured by the estimated beta. The event window analysis assumes that any systematic deviation from expected returns around the announcement can be attributed to the investigation news.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s59_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using market model
# Abnormal return = Actual return - Expected return
# Expected return = beta * market return
data <- data %>%
  mutate(expected_ret = beta * mkt_ret,
         abnormal_ret = ret - expected_ret)

# Define event windows
estimation_window <- data %>% filter(event_day >= -30 & event_day <= -11)
event_window <- data %>% filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1)
post_event <- data %>% filter(event_day >= 2 & event_day <= 10)

# Calculate daily average abnormal returns across all stocks
daily_aar <- data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(aar = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
            se = sd(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
            t_stat = aar / se,
            p_value = 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n() - 1, lower.tail = FALSE),
            .groups = 'drop')

# Calculate CAR for each stock in event window (-1, +1)
car_by_stock <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_3day = sum(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = 'drop')

# Calculate overall CAR statistics
car_stats <- car_by_stock %>%
  summarise(mean_car = mean(car_3day),
            se_car = sd(car_3day) / sqrt(n()),
            t_stat = mean_car / se_car,
            p_value = 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n() - 1, lower.tail = FALSE),
            n_stocks = n())

# Print main results
cat("=== SEC Investigation Announcement Event Study Results ===\n\n")
cat("3-Day CAR (-1, +1) Results:\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean CAR: %.4f (%.2f%%)\n", car_stats$mean_car, car_stats$mean_car * 100))
cat(sprintf("Standard Error: %.4f\n", car_stats$se_car))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic: %.3f\n", car_stats$t_stat))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", car_stats$p_value))
cat(sprintf("Number of stocks: %d\n\n", car_stats$n_stocks))

# Print daily AAR around event
cat("Daily Average Abnormal Returns:\n")
event_period <- daily_aar %>% filter(event_day >= -5 & event_day <= 5)
for(i in 1:nrow(event_period)) {
  row <- event_period[i,]
  significance <- ifelse(row$p_value < 0.01, "***", 
                        ifelse(row$p_value < 0.05, "**", 
                              ifelse(row$p_value < 0.1, "*", "")))
  cat(sprintf("Day %2d: AAR = %7.4f, t-stat = %6.3f %s\n", 
              row$event_day, row$aar, row$t_stat, significance))
}

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== Robustness Checks ===\n")

# 1. Alternative event windows
car_1day <- data %>%
  filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  summarise(mean_car = mean(abnormal_ret),
            se = sd(abnormal_ret) / sqrt(n()),
            t_stat = mean_car / se,
            p_value = 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n() - 1, lower.tail = FALSE))

car_5day <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -2 & event_day <= 2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_5day = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  summarise(mean_car = mean(car_5day),
            se = sd(car_5day) / sqrt(n()),
            t_stat = mean_car / se,
            p_value = 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n() - 1, lower.tail = FALSE))

cat(sprintf("1-Day CAR (0): %.4f, t-stat: %.3f, p-value: %.4f\n", 
            car_1day$mean_car, car_1day$t_stat, car_1day$p_value))
cat(sprintf("5-Day CAR (-2,+2): %.4f, t-stat: %.3f, p-value: %.4f\n", 
            car_5day$mean_car, car_5day$t_stat, car_5day$p_value))

# 2. Test for pre-event drift
pre_event_car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(pre_car = sum(abnormal_ret), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  summarise(mean_car = mean(pre_car),
            se = sd(pre_car) / sqrt(n()),
            t_stat = mean_car / se,
            p_value = 2 * pt(abs(t_stat), df = n() - 1, lower.tail = FALSE))

cat(sprintf("Pre-event CAR (-10,-2): %.4f, t-stat: %.3f, p-value: %.4f\n", 
            pre_event_car$mean_car, pre_event_car$t_stat, pre_event_car$p_value))

# 3. Cross-sectional test
cat(sprintf("\nCross-sectional variation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("Min CAR: %.4f, Max CAR: %.4f\n", 
            min(car_by_stock$car_3day), max(car_by_stock$car_3day)))
cat(sprintf("Proportion negative CARs: %.2f%%\n", 
            mean(car_by_stock$car_3day < 0) * 100))

# Statistical significance summary
if(car_stats$p_value < 0.01) {
  cat("\n*** Result is statistically significant at 1% level ***\n")
} else if(car_stats$p_value < 0.05) {
  cat("\n** Result is statistically significant at 5% level **\n")
} else if(car_stats$p_value < 0.1) {
  cat("\n* Result is statistically significant at 10% level *\n")
} else {
  cat("\nResult is not statistically significant\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect to find a significantly negative CAR around SEC investigation announcements, likely in the range of -2% to -5% over the 3-day event window (-1, +1). The negative reaction should be most pronounced on the announcement day (day 0) with possible information leakage on day -1. The market reaction reflects investors' concerns about potential legal costs, regulatory penalties, reputational damage, and increased uncertainty about the company's future performance. The effect should be statistically significant given that SEC investigations represent material adverse news that directly impacts firm value and investor confidence.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy relies on comparing stock returns around the SEC investigation announcement day.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The announcement of an SEC investigation is associated with a positive change in cumulative abnormal returns.
